tagline: Hanksville to Blanding, crossing the Colorado once at Hite.
intro: At the east edge of Hanksville, Highway 24 hooks north and Highway 95 turns south, signed for Hite. The Henry Mountains stand off to the west, Mount Ellen first and then Mount Pennell. Below the Ticaboo fork the road winds through a redrock canyon whose walls are not especially high but are carved and pockmarked all over, and then the canyon opens out above the water of Lake Powell.

Until the 1970s this was mostly a dirt road. It was paved for the national Bicentennial and dedicated in 1976, replacing a trip of several days over dirt tracks and river ferries, and the name stayed with it.

moments.title: Little Egypt
moments.text: The big mesa off to the right going south was named by early cowboys, who were reminded of the Sphinx.

moments.title: Hite Crossing Bridge
moments.text: An arch bridge of 1966 now carries the road a little upstream of where travelers once used Cass Hite's ford and later a ferry driven by an old car engine, both lost to Lake Powell.

moments.title: Fry Canyon
moments.text: A uranium boom town of the 1950s, now a ghost town, whose lodge opened in 1955 and closed in 2007.

practical: Fill up in Hanksville. Capitol Reef Country counts no services on the 120 miles to Blanding, and Visit Utah lists only limited services at Hite Marina.
